Surah 103: Al-'Asr (The Time)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By the time⁠—﴾ He swore by the prayer of 'Asr (al-'Asr), because of its excellence, as evidenced by His saying (Exalted is He): "And the middle prayer, the prayer of 'Asr" (al-Salah al-Wusta), in the codex of Hafsah. And because the obligation to perform it is more difficult, owing to people's preoccupation with their trades and earnings at the end of the day and their busyness with their livelihoods. Or He swore by the evening (al-'ashiyy), just as He swore by the forenoon (al-duha), because of the signs of power in it. Or He swore by time (al-zaman), because of the many kinds of wonders in its passing. And the answer to the oath is:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 103, verse 2:

﴿Indeed, mankind is surely in loss﴾. That is: the species of mankind is surely in loss in their trade (tijarat, "commercial dealings").

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 103, verse 3:

﴿Except those who have believed and done righteous deeds﴾, for they have bought the Hereafter with the worldly life, so they profited and were made happy.

﴿And advised one another to the truth﴾, that is, to the matter that is established and firm, whose denial is not permissible, and which is all good: from the Oneness of Allah, obedience to Him, and following His Books and His Messengers.

﴿And advised one another to patience﴾, that is, to refrain from sins, or to persevere in acts of obedience, and to endure what Allah tests His servants with. And "tawasaw" (they advised one another), in both places, is a past-tense verb (fi'l madi), conjoined (ma'tuf) upon the past-tense verb before it.
